# goguma

> A free, open-source macOS menu bar app that wakes a sleeping Mac shortly
> before each scheduled job is due, holds sleep off while the job runs, and
> lets the machine sleep again once it finishes. It also keeps a coding agent
> working with the lid closed. Requires macOS 14 or later, or Linux with
> systemd. MIT licensed.

goguma does not run your jobs. Your existing scheduler still fires them —
goguma makes sure the machine is awake when they do. A sleeping Mac does not
queue the jobs it missed and catch up later; cron skips them outright, with no
error written anywhere, which is why the failure usually goes unnoticed for
weeks. (launchd is different: it re-fires a missed `StartCalendarInterval` job
on wake, and goguma leaves those alone.)

## What makes it different from caffeinate, Amphetamine and pmset

- **They can only keep an awake machine awake. goguma can wake a sleeping
  one.** It schedules real OS wakes with `pmset schedule` for jobs it found by
  reading your existing schedulers.
- **`pmset -a disablesleep 1` is a global switch with no owner.** It persists
  in the power management preferences even if the process that set it is
  killed, so nothing ever turns it back off. goguma's holds are leases that
  expire on their own, and its privileged helper clears a stranded block after
  60 seconds without contact.
- **caffeinate holds sleep off only with the lid open.** Close the lid on
  battery and the Mac sleeps through the job anyway.

goguma uses `pmset` itself — `pmset -a disablesleep` and `pmset schedule`. The
part that is not pmset is knowing what to arm, when, and when to refuse.

## Where jobs come from

It reads schedulers you already have: `crontab`, user and system launchd jobs,
and Hermes. Apps that keep their own schedule store can be described to it with
a JSON manifest. You define nothing.

## Coding agents

Hooks are installed automatically for Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor and
Gemini CLI, so those report when they are working and the Mac stays awake until
they stop. Any other agent or long command can be wrapped:
`goguma run -- <command>`. The hold lasts exactly as long as that command.

Agent activity cannot be detected by watching processes: an agent waiting on a
model is blocked on a socket and looks identical to an idle one. The work is
not local, so the harness has to say so.

## Safety

- Holds expire by themselves: 90 seconds for a wrapped command without renewal,
  15 minutes for an agent session, 12 hours maximum however often renewed.
- With the lid closed, every hold is dropped if the machine gets hot or the
  battery falls below the cutout — the state where a machine in a bag cannot
  show you anything is wrong.
- It refuses to schedule a wake at all when the battery cannot afford the job,
  because a cutout cannot un-wake a machine once the energy is spent. The
  margin is the job's own measured drain, not a flat number.

## Privacy

No telemetry, no analytics, no crash reporting, no account. Jobs, history and
settings stay in `~/Library/Application Support/goguma`. The only request it
makes is fetching a signed advisory feed, sent with no User-Agent beyond the Go
runtime's default, no query string and no cookies. A webhook is sent only if
you configure one.

## Security

Four binaries, one of which runs as root. The privileged helper answers six
messages and holds no policy; everything else runs unprivileged. All binaries
are signed with a Developer ID and notarised by Apple, and setup names who
signed the helper before asking for your password, refusing to install it if
that signature cannot be verified.

## Install

Download [goguma.dmg](https://github.com/junnam586/goguma/releases/latest/download/goguma.dmg),
drag it to Applications and open it. Or `brew install junnam586/tap/goguma`
followed by `goguma install` for the command line tools alone.
